1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. VPN: virtual private network

  • A method to diagnose a weak output: observe, isolate, change one thing, test
  • A symptom to cause to fix table for the most common problems
  • How to troubleshoot features, files and errors
  • How to use feedback to adjust your approach

2A Diagnostic Method

Running case

Cedarbrook's Disappointing Replies

  • Care agents complain that Claude's reply drafts are too long, too stiff and sometimes quote the wrong policy
  • The team lead does not rewrite everything. They collect five bad examples, find the pattern and change one thing at a time

  1. Observe: what exactly is wrong? Save the prompt and the bad output.
  2. Find the pattern: is it every time, or only for some inputs? Compare good and bad cases.
  3. Hypothesize the cause: missing context, unclear instruction, conflicting rules, wrong feature, stale knowledge, wrong model, or a limit.
  4. Change one thing: a clearer instruction, an example, a source file, a different feature or model.
  5. Test on the same inputs and compare. Keep what works; log it.
  • Changing many things at once hides which change helped.
  • Test on several cases, including awkward ones, not only the one that failed.
Exam tip

The expected approach is systematic and minimal: diagnose the cause, change one variable, retest. Starting over completely, or switching to the biggest model first, is usually not the best answer.

3Symptoms, Causes and Fixes

Symptom Likely cause Fix
Generic or vague answer Missing goal, audience, context Add purpose, audience, facts, an example (Module 1)
Wrong format or length Format not specified State structure, word count, fields; give an example
Ignores a rule Rule buried, vague, conflicting, or too many rules Put it clearly and early; explain why; remove conflicts; shorten the list
Invented facts or sources No source provided; Claude fills gaps Provide the source; ask to quote it; allow "not covered"; verify (Modules 3 and 4)
Outdated information Knowledge cutoff Use web search; check dates
Forgets earlier instructions; repeats itself Long, drifted context Summarize and restart; move standing rules into a Project (Modules 8 and 11)
Inconsistent tone across outputs No voice reference Add examples, a style or Project instructions
Shallow reasoning on a hard task Task too big for one step, or light model or low effort Break into steps; use thinking; try a stronger model or higher effort
Misreads a document Poor file type, scanned pages, large file Check file type and limits; split; ask for quotes; try text version
Spreadsheet or script fails Untested output, wrong tool version Test on a sample; give the exact error message back to Claude; state your tool and version
Claims it did something it could not (sent an email, saved a file) No integration exists Check the destination; enable the connector or do the step yourself
Links do not work Produced from memory Open every link; ask for sources and verify
Refuses a legitimate request Wording looks like a prohibited request, or context is missing Explain the legitimate purpose and context; rephrase; if truly restricted, follow policy
Biased or one-sided Leading prompt or skewed data Ask for balance; neutral wording; check data (Module 3)
Too slow / limit reached Heavy tools, high effort, long chat Lower effort, lighter model, new chat (Module 16)

4Feature, File and Error Problems

Problem Check
Web search not used Is it available and on? Say "search the web"; on Team and Enterprise the owner must enable it
Research seems inactive Prompt directly: "please use the research tool"; web search must be on; on mobile connectors are skipped
Skill not applied Skills need code execution on; toggle the skill on; the description must say when to use it; be explicit in the request
Skills section greyed out Code execution (Create and edit files) is off for you or your organization
Spreadsheet (XLSX) upload fails XLSX needs code execution and file creation turned on
File too large or too long Chat limits: 500 MB per file, 20 files, PDFs up to 1,000 pages; split documents
Connector not pulling data Reconnect from Customize > Connectors; confirm you have access; use web or Desktop (not mobile) for Research with connectors
"Message will exceed the length limit" Attach fewer or smaller files, split or summarize, or start a new chat
"Approaching" or "reached" usage limit Wait for the five-hour or weekly reset, reduce usage, or use credits if enabled
"Due to unexpected capacity constraints" System-wide demand, not your fault; wait a few minutes and retry
Login error Turn off VPN and extensions, clear cache and cookies, check the status page
Output blocked by content filtering Rephrase the request; check it is within the Usage Policy

5Using Feedback and Results

  • Collect feedback from users: what failed, how often, in what situation. Use real examples, not impressions.
  • Thumbs-down a bad response to report it; it helps improve the product but does not fix your prompt.
  • Adjust the layer where the cause lies: prompt (wording), Project (instructions, knowledge), skill (method), model or effort, feature (search, Research, files), or process (add a review step).
  • Measure before and after: error rate, time to finish, satisfaction (Module 16).
  • Share what you learn: update the prompt library and instructions so others benefit.
  • Know when to stop or escalate: if the same task fails after clear prompts, correct knowledge and a stronger model, the task may be a poor fit, or it may need a Developer's help (Module 10).
Exam tip

Change one thing at a time and retest: changing everything at once hides what worked.

Exam tip

If Claude says it did something (sent, saved, booked), check the destination before you trust it.

6Exam Q&A

S1A team's reply drafts keep running too long. What is the best first change?

  • ATurn off all features
  • BSwitch to the largest model, since a bigger model always follows length instructions without being told
  • CSpecify the length and structure (under 120 words: greeting, answer, next step) and give an example
  • DStart every chat from scratch
Show the answer

Answer: C. Format and length problems usually come from an unspecified format; fix the prompt first.

S2Claude keeps quoting the wrong return window. The Project contains two policy versions. What should the owner do?

  • ARemove the outdated file so only the current policy remains, then retest
  • BAdd a third version of the policy file so that Claude can compare all three versions
  • CDelete the instructions and let Claude work out the correct return window by itself
  • DTell Claude to guess
Show the answer

Answer: A. Conflicting knowledge is a likely cause; fix the source and test.

S3An analyst changes the model, the prompt, the files and the settings all at once, and the output improves. What is the weakness of this approach?

  • AIt is too fast
  • BIt uses too little usage
  • CThey cannot tell which change helped, so the result is hard to reproduce or explain
  • DNone
Show the answer

Answer: C. Change one variable at a time to learn what works.

S4Claude says it emailed a supplier, but no email integration is connected. What is the best response?

  • ADelete the chat
  • BVerify, send the email yourself or set up the approved connector, and treat the claim as unreliable
  • CAssume the supplier received it, because Claude would not state that an email was sent unless it was
  • DAsk Claude to repeat the claim
Show the answer

Answer: B. Claude can overstate its abilities; check the destination.

S5A custom skill is installed but Claude never uses it. What should you check first?

  • AThe color of the skill icon
  • BWhether the skill is switched on, code execution is enabled, and its description says when to use it
  • CWhether you are on mobile
  • DWhether the model name contains the word "skill", because only those models can use skills at all in the app
Show the answer

Answer: B. A skill that is off, a disabled code execution setting or a vague description are the documented reasons Claude does not use it.

S6Which TWO are good responses to a long chat that has started to contradict itself? Select TWO.

  • AMove standing rules into a Project's instructions
  • BAsk for a summary of decisions and continue in a new chat
  • CKeep adding messages
  • DRemove the rules entirely
  • EAsk for the same answer repeatedly
Show the answer

Answer: A, B. Restart with a summary and persist the rules properly.

S7A spreadsheet formula from Claude returns an error in Google Sheets. What is the best next step?

  • AApply it to all of the data anyway, because the error probably affects only a few rows and Sheets will skip them
  • BPaste the exact error message and a data sample back to Claude, state the tool, and test the fix on a few rows
  • CAbandon formulas
  • DAsk for a longer explanation
Show the answer

Answer: B. Give Claude the evidence and test the fix on a small sample.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Method Observe · pattern · cause · change one thing · test · record
Generic output Add context, audience, example
Ignored rule Clearer, earlier, with a reason; fewer rules
Invented facts Provide the source; quote; allow "not covered"; verify
Forgetful Summarize and restart; Project for standing rules
Tone drift Examples, style, Project instructions
Shallow reasoning Steps, thinking, stronger model or effort
Claimed actions Check the destination; enable the connector or do it yourself
Feature fails Check the toggle, plan, code execution, limits, description
Feedback Use real examples; adjust the right layer; measure; share lessons
